function.mechanism: Dissociates into calcium and sulfate ions; calcium promotes structure-setting in protein/polysaccharide matrices and sulfate contributes ionic strength.
common_food_categories: tofu and soy curd coagulant systems

adi.basis: EFSA (2019) concluded there is no need for a numerical ADI for sulfuric acid and sulfate salts including E516 at reported uses and use levels.

efsa.key_finding: Exposure to E513/E514/E515/E516/E517 at reported uses did not raise a safety concern; estimated sulfate exposure was far below the human dose associated with laxative effects.

fda.notes: Direct-food GRAS affirmation with GMP/category limits in 21 CFR 184.1230; animal-feed GRAS listing also present at 21 CFR 582.5230.

adi.basis: WHO JECFA database lists ADI as NOT LIMITED for calcium sulfate.

concerns.summary: At sufficiently high sulfate doses, osmotic/laxative gastrointestinal effects can occur in humans; EFSA used a human laxative-effect reference point well above modeled additive exposure.
Impurity management is a regulatory caveat: EFSA recommended lowering arsenic, lead, and mercury limits in EU specifications for sulfate additives including E516.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2019 concluded no safety concern for reported uses and use levels of sulfate additives including E516.
EFSA reported no concern for genotoxicity and carcinogenicity in the evaluated sulfate dataset.
JECFA ADI status is NOT LIMITED for calcium sulfate.
U.S. direct-food use is affirmed as GRAS in 21 CFR 184.1230.

populations: toddlers (highest modeled sulfate exposure in EFSA scenarios)
individuals with unusually high therapeutic/supplemental sulfate intake
adi_exceedance.notes: No numerical ADI is set by EFSA/JECFA for this group; EFSA exposure estimates for sulfate from food additive use were far below the cited human laxative-effect dose.

risk_assessment.rationale: Current regulatory evidence is consistently permissive (EFSA approved/no numerical ADI needed, FDA GRAS, JECFA NOT LIMITED), with no identified IARC carcinogenic classification for calcium sulfate. Observed concerns are mainly high-dose GI effects and impurity-specification management rather than demonstrated harm at modeled dietary additive exposure.
key_factors: EFSA 2019 no-safety-concern conclusion at reported uses and use levels
EFSA and JECFA non-numerical ADI positioning
FDA GRAS status with defined CFR conditions of use
No calcium sulfate entry found in current IARC classified-agent dataset
Modeled dietary exposure substantially below human laxative-effect reference dose
